key_insight: VGGT-Edit performs native 3D scene edits in a single feed‑forward pass by predicting a residual 3D field that locally modifies an underlying neural scene representation, yielding multi‑view consistent, instruction-driven changes without per-edit optimization.
problem_solved: Overcomes reliance on 2D‑lifting and slow per‑edit optimization that produce inconsistent multi‑view results; enables fast, consistent, interactive 3D scene editing from human instructions.
method: Operate directly on a learned 3D scene representation and predict a residual field (geometry +/or appearance) that encodes the requested edit
Use a feed‑forward model conditioned on the scene, edit instruction and edit region to produce a single-pass update to the neural field, preserving global consistency
Design loss/training strategy to localize edits, retain unedited content, and generalize across scenes so edits are immediate and multi‑view coherent
impact: Enables real‑time, instruction-driven 3D scene editing that is consistent across views and easy to integrate into interactive pipelines—reducing latency and manual tuning for downstream AR/VR, simulation, and content creation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input scene + textual/painted instruction → feed‑forward residual field predictor → edited 3D neural field → rendered multi‑view outputs
Before/After multi‑view gallery showing consistent edits from multiple camera angles versus inconsistent 2D‑lift baselines
Bar chart comparing edit latency and multi‑view coherence (consistency score) between VGGT‑Edit and optimization‑based methods
Icon set: single‑pass (speedometer), multi‑view consistency (camera cluster), local preservation (shield) to emphasize practical benefits
paper_title: VGGT-Edit: Feed-forward Native 3D Scene Editing with Residual Field Prediction
paper_authors: Kaixin Zhu, Yiwen Tang, Yifan Yang, Renrui Zhang, Bohan Zeng
